chapter: Leading his own band in Los Angeles
title: Les Hite's Cotton Club band and Paul Howard's Quality Serenaders
summary: He compares Les Hite's Cotton Club band and its stars with his own, and mentions Paul Howard's earlier band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Oh, so you were really an established band?
Yes, well there were only two bands at the time. You see we lost Parker Berry.
He went to join Les Hite. Now, Les Hite was working at the Cotton Club. They had

the best job. And that's when I met Louis, was in '32. The first time I ever seen Louis and he was working at the Cotton Club. It was the big club. They made more money. And Fats Waller had played the Cotton Club with Les Hite. Les Hite was the home band.
And they would come in as sort of guest stars?

Yes. Now Les had Marshall Royal in his band. He had Lawrence Brown in his band. He had Lionel Hampton in his band. He had the big names. Where I think we had, we had the best band. Because we had a battle with them one time and I know we won, everybody said we won.
Well that must have been a good band then.
It was a good band. We had some very nice......
Well where were Paul Howard and the Quality Serendders then?.
Well, they were a little earlier than that. They played for dances in the park.
And Lionel was in that band too. But see this was about 1929.
I'd say about '29. They played for a lot of dances and they had some wonderful recordings out. Wonderful recordings.
Yes, they were on 'Victor' so they had good distribution.
Yes, right. Paul is still out there, he is in the Union now. Still in the Union.
